brief: AI chip stocks fell (Philadelphia semi index down 5.9%, North Asia memory names down mid-single digits) after frontier labs publicly backed pacing development of the most advanced models, amid closed-door talks on an industry safety standards body, departing-researcher warnings, a bipartisan US Senate AI-rules push, new California AI-auditor standards, and Trump calling misuse fears a hoax. UBS argues pacing does not mean lower capex: inference, the larger share of AI compute demand, is gated by enterprise adoption rather than model capability, while training keeps going, so UBS retains its 2027 AI industry capex forecast of $1.2tr, up 33% from $900bn this year, citing continued Grok 4.8 training and OpenAI's reiterated growth expectations. UBS also argues tighter safety rules could reshape competition toward large incumbents and away from startups, and notes the selloff hit AI stocks at lower valuations (SOXX near 21x forward earnings versus 33x in June) with earnings still growing fast, so UBS stays diversified across the AI value chain rather than cutting exposure. Separately, the 10-year Treasury yield topped 5% for the first time since 2023 ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision; UBS still favors holding quality bonds for income and resilience.
